core_meaning.short_meaning: Noble little lion; prominent companion Usayd ibn Hudayr al-Ansari.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Usayd (أُسَيْد) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning 'noble young lion' or 'little lion' (diminutive of asad). In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of the noble companion Usayd ibn Hudayr al-Ansari, a chief of the Aws tribe whose Quran recitation brought angels down from the heavens.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Diminutive form of the Arabic noun asad (lion), conveying endearment, valor, and spirited courage.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root ʾ-s-d denotes courage, boldness, and the lion in classical Arabic lexicography. As a proper name, it was carried by Usayd ibn Hudayr al-Ashhali, one of the leaders of the Ansar who pledged allegiance at the Second Pledge of al-Aqaba and fought at Badr and Uhud. When he recited Surah al-Baqarah at night, lights descended from the sky, which the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ identified as angels.
